correctedState:
`SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS` (packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:183) is `['disabled','allowRead','allowManagedReadPathsOnly']`, and the doc's other three path keys live flat at the top of the `sandbox` object under different names — `filesystem.allowWrite`→`additionalWritableRoots`, `filesystem.denyWrite`→`deniedWriteRoots`, `filesystem.denyRead`→`deniedReadRoots` (`SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS`, :172–:180). `filesystemSection` (:267) throws `invalid sandbox filesystem setting: allowWrite` on any other nested key — reproduced by running the parser.

Three corrections to the stated consequence:

- SCOPES. There is no "user/project/local" tier here. This fork composes exactly two sandbox layers (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/host-sandbox-settings.ts:69): the managed-policy floor and one user layer. There is no project or local sandbox scope at all.

- WHICH FILE. The user layer is not Claude's `.claude/settings.json` — it is Nessy's own `~/.nessy-agent/config.json`, read by `getUserSandboxSettings` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:1293). Nessy touches `.claude/settings.json` only as a permission-rule writer (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts). So the exposure is "an admin or user porting a documented Claude sandbox stanza into Nessy's config gets it silently dropped", not "Claude's settings file is rejected".

- "REJECTED WHOLE" is right at user scope but only for the `sandbox` layer, and it is not an app failure: `getUserSandboxSettings` catches the throw, logs "Invalid `sandbox` in the user config — the layer is rejected whole and ignored" (storage.ts:1239) and returns `{}`; the rest of `config.json` survives. At MANAGED scope nothing throws — the tolerant sink strips per key. Parsing the doc's own example stanza tolerantly yields drops `sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite` → stripped and `sandbox.filesystem.denyRead` → stripped, while `excludedCommands` and the whole `network` block still apply. So the managed half degrades silently and partially, which is arguably the worse of the two: an administrator's write/read boundary vanishes with a diagnostic and the rest of the policy still loads, looking applied.

Two adjacent divergences the row understates, both from the same probe:

- The doc's example stanza fails on FOUR keys, not two: `sandbox.enabled` and `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` are rejected/stripped as well (neither is in `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS`). At user scope the strict parse throws on `enabled` before it ever reaches `filesystem`.

- The quoted sentence is about PATH PREFIXES, and those diverge too. `filesystemRoots` demands absolute paths, so the doc's `~/` and `./` prefixes — the exact subject of the cited line, and used in the doc's own examples `~/.kube` and `./output` — are refused: `~/.kube` → `sandbox-additionalWritableRoots-not-absolute`, `./output` → same. Only `/tmp/build` is accepted. A row scoped to key names alone misses that the prefix contract the sentence actually specifies is unimplemented in every one of these keys.
